vendor: arXiv, Inc. (Cornell University Library before July 1, 2026)
product_family: Free, open-access preprint repository for scholarly articles in physics, mathematics, computer science, quantitative biology, finance, statistics, electrical engineering, and economics. ~2.4 million papers, ~24,000 monthly submissions. Recently spun off from Cornell University as an independent nonprofit.

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type 1
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of SOC 2 Type 1 certification. Privacy policy and public documentation make no reference to SOC 2 compliance.

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type 2
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of SOC 2 Type 2 certification. No security audit or ongoing controls attestation mentioned in any vendor documentation.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of ISO 27001 certification. No information security management system certification mentioned.

certifications.name: GDPR Compliance
certifications.proof_quote: While privacy policy mentions data handling, no GDPR compliance claim or Data Processing Agreement (DPA) is offered. Vendor serves global EU researchers without explicit GDPR certification.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of HIPAA compliance. arXiv is a preprint repository with no health/medical compliance certifications.

certifications.name: ISO 27017 (Cloud Security)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Cloud security controls not certified.

certifications.name: ISO 27018 (PII Protection)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. PII protection controls not certified.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of FedRAMP authorization. arXiv is a nonprofit with no federal government security certification.

privacy.ai_training_note: Submission agreement does not explicitly restrict or permit AI training on submitted papers. Vendor claims no AI training use in current documentation, but this critical gap creates ambiguity during industry-wide LLM training debates. Authors' papers may be used for research purposes via anonymized data sharing with 'trusted partners' but explicit AI training policy is absent.
privacy.data_region: United States (Cornell Tech HQ, New York City). Service providers used for hosting and data processing; specific regions not disclosed.

security.name: Encryption in Transit
security.value: HTTPS standard mentioned in privacy policy as 'standard practices,' but no specific TLS version, cipher suite, or implementation details disclosed.

security.name: Encryption at Rest
security.value: Not mentioned. No disclosure of encryption methods for stored data.

security.name: Access Controls
security.value: Privacy policy mentions 'detecting fraud and preventing unauthorized access, including DDoS attacks,' but no details on authentication, authorization, or role-based access controls.

security.name: Incident Response
security.value: No incident response policy or breach notification timeline disclosed.

security.name: Security Audit / Penetration Testing
security.value: No third-party security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessment programs disclosed.

security.name: Data Minimization
security.value: arXiv collects author names, affiliations, email addresses, and submission metadata—all of which are made publicly available by design. User registration data retained up to 1 year.

security.name: Anonymization / De-identification
security.value: Anonymized research data deleted after 5 years. No disclosure of anonymization techniques or reversibility risks.

products.name: arXiv Preprint Repository
products.data_scope: Author names, affiliations, email addresses, submitted manuscripts (permanent public archive), submission metadata, user registration data
products.notes: Free to use and submit. Data is permanently archived in the public interest. No registration required to read. No payment model; supported by member institutions and the Simons Foundation.

products.name: arXivLabs (Research Partnerships)
products.data_scope: Anonymized manuscript data shared with research partners for search and discovery tools (e.g., NASA Astrophysics Data System)
products.notes: Partners must adhere to privacy and ethical standards. Data shared is anonymized; specific retention and usage terms per partner agreement (not publicly detailed).

compare.pricing_model: Free to read and submit. Nonprofit funding model: member institutions + Simons Foundation support. Membership program allows libraries and research labs to contribute financially.
compare.data_residency: United States (Cornell Tech, New York City). Service providers' locations not disclosed.

flags: arXiv spun off from Cornell on July 1, 2026, and as of July 6, 2026 the standalone organization was only 5 days old. It is legally newly established, and its governance, compliance, and security infrastructure may not yet be fully operational.

There is no explicit policy prohibiting AI training on submitted papers. The submission agreement grants a 'non-exclusive, perpetual' license for 'machine-readable formats' but does not address LLM training use, which leaves the question ambiguous amid industry-wide AI training data controversies.
arXiv holds zero SOC 2, ISO 27001, or equivalent third-party security certifications despite handling global scholarly data.
No Data Processing Agreement is offered despite arXiv serving thousands of EU researchers, and there is no explicit GDPR compliance claim.
Security disclosures are thin: the privacy policy states only 'standard practices' without specifics on encryption, key management, audit trails, or incident response.
There is no evidence of third-party security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability review programs.
arXiv's core model requires public disclosure of author names, affiliations, and emails. While necessary for the scholarly record, this increases the privacy surface.
Data is shared with 'trusted partners' and service providers for hosting and processing, but the specific vendors, locations, and contractual security terms are not publicly detailed.
The new nonprofit board structure (12 members) and interim CEO mean governance is still being established, and a long-term security strategy and compliance roadmap have not been communicated.

As a new IRS 501(c)(3) entity, arXiv must file Form 990-N annually but has not yet done so; the organization is less than 6 months old. Its tax-exempt status is verified, but financial transparency reports are still to come.
